in_english.name: Moutaaz
in_english.long_meaning: Moutaaz is a masculine given name of Arabic origin, derived from the root 'ع-ز-م' which conveys meanings of strength, power, and protection. In Islamic tradition, the name signifies one who is protected by God, strong and unyielding. The name has been used across various Muslim cultures, reflecting its significance in Islamic heritage and its association with positive attributes such as resilience and fortitude

data.cultural_impact: The name Moutaaz carries significant cultural importance in the Islamic community. As one who persists and remains determined, individuals named Moutaaz are often seen as strong leaders, trailblazers and individuals who tirelessly work towards their goals. In various Islamic societies and communities, this name is associated with strength, resilience and an unyielding spirit that does not give in to adversity.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Moutaaz holds deep meaning and importance in the Islamic faith. It is a name that echoes the qualities of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) who, despite facing numerous challenges and adversities, never wavered in his faith or commitment to spreading the message of Islam. Moutaaz also has parallels with the Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) in the Quran, who despite being wrongfully imprisoned and forgotten, never lost hope and was eventually vindicated and elevated to a position of power and prestige. As such, the spiritual significance of the name Moutaaz is one that inspires faith, determination, and unwavering commitment to one's beliefs and goals.

historical_references.context: Moutaaz ibn Abi Ar-Rabah Al-Qushayri: He was a poet from the city of Kufa. He is reported to have had a deep knowledge of the Quran and the Prophetic Sunnah. He was a contemporary of the sixth and seventh Caliphs of Islam. He was known for his eloquence and his ability to express the truths of faith through poetry. Moutaaz was also a great debater and is said to have engaged in debates with prominent scholars of his time to defend Islam against their criticisms.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Maqrizi's Al-Khitat Al-Khawayriyah The name Moutaaz carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Moutaaz ibn Abdallah Al-Fasawi: He was a prominent scholar of Islamic jurisprudence, hadith, and poetry from the city of Fas (present-day Morocco). He was born in the late 13th century during the Marinid dynasty and studied under several prominent scholars of his time. He is best known for his works on the Maliki school of Islamic jurisprudence and his poetry, which reflects his deep knowledge of the Quran and the Prophetic Sunnah.
